references.text: The Lord's promise to Abraham to give the land to his descendants, as referenced in Exodus 33:1.
God's promise to Isaac to give the land to his offspring, a confirmation of the covenant with Abraham.
God's promise to Jacob regarding the land, confirming the promise given to Abraham and Isaac.
Joseph reminds the children of Israel of God's promise to bring them out of Egypt to the promised land.
The Lord tells Moses that He has come down to deliver the people from Egypt and lead them to a good land.
Moses reminds God of the promise made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to give their descendants the land.
The Lord swears that the disobedient generation will not see the land promised to the fathers.
Moses reminds the people that the Lord has given them the land He swore to give to the fathers.
The Lord shows Moses the land and reminds him of the promise made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Abraham's faith in the promise of the land is mentioned as an example of faith in the New Testament.
Exodus 32:7 sets the scene for Exodus 33:1 by showing that God's command to go to the land comes immediately after the people break the covenant.
Exodus 6:8 establishes the promise as the basis for the command given in Exodus 33:1, demonstrating God's faithfulness throughout the journey.
Deuteronomy 31:16 sheds light on Exodus 33:1 by revealing the tragic irony that the people will go to the land yet still abandon God's covenant there.
Deuteronomy 31:7 shows the transition from Moses' leadership in Exodus 33:1 to Joshua's leadership to fulfill the promise of the land.
Numbers 27:12 illuminates Exodus 33:1 by showing the tragic conclusion of Moses' journey: he is allowed to see the land he was commanded to go toward in Exodus 33:1, but will not enter it.
